results.summary: This Wokwi design uses a small network of OR and AND gates to drive a seven-segment display. When switches 0 or 1 are turned on, the digit 2 is displayed; turning on switches 5 and 6 shows a decimal point. The author states they are unsure how the remaining inputs and outputs behave, and the project has no test procedure or external hardware listed. Documentation is minimal and partly contradictory, making the exact gate mapping unverifiable.

This design connects each of the eight inputs to an inverter whose output drives a corresponding indicator on a clock. The intended use is to set the inputs and observe whether the matching light turns on, effectively demonstrating inversion. It requires an external clock as the display hardware. The documentation is very brief and the pin names are the main source of information about the function.

This project implements AND, NAND and OR logic on two DIP-switch inputs and shows the results on a seven-segment display. A step button or an external 10 kHz clock advances the registered logic state, and a reset button clears it. The documentation includes a full truth table and a step-by-step test procedure, making it a teaching aid for basic gates. It is a Wokwi design with no additional external hardware beyond the display and switches.

This Wokwi project is a simple OR gate test circuit with inputs and outputs exposed on the chip pins. The description says it tests OR gates and that it is verified through the inputs and outputs, but the included truth table is incomplete and mislabeled. No external hardware is required. Documentation is thin and the pin names are inconsistent, so the exact wiring is unclear.

This design uses eight switches routed through four AND gates whose outputs feed two OR gates, each controlling four segments of a seven-segment display. The description presents it as a basic AND/OR demonstration, and testing consists of exercising the switches. No external hardware is listed. The documentation is short and the segment mapping is not fully specified.

This project connects each of the eight inputs to an inverter that drives a corresponding light on a clock. The intended test is to set an input and check that the inverted output appears, as shown in the single-row truth table. An external clock is required as the display. The documentation is minimal and largely duplicates the pin names.

This Wokwi project appears to connect eight inputs to eight outputs, with the same signals also exposed on the bidirectional pins. The description, test instructions and external hardware fields all say the author does not know, so the actual behavior cannot be determined from the documentation. No test procedure or hardware requirements are given. The design is essentially undocumented beyond its pin names.

This design routes switches through AND gates, inverters and direct wires to corresponding outputs, as indicated by the pin names. The description only states that it connects a switch to a light, and testing is done by using the switch. No external hardware is required. Documentation is very sparse, so the exact gate arrangement is inferred from the pin labels.

This combinational design feeds four pairs of inputs through XOR gates, combines those results with two AND gates, and passes the final result through an XNOR gate to all eight outputs. The intended test is to set all inputs low, or to set one input of each pair high and the other low, and confirm the outputs are asserted in both cases. No external hardware is needed. The documentation is clear about the gate topology but does not explain a practical application.

This project is titled gds and described only as gds creation, with no explanation of its function. The pins are labeled with letters and numbers, and the bidirectional pins are numbered 1 through 8, but the documentation gives no behavior, test method or hardware requirements. The author explicitly says to figure it out and does not know how to test it. There is essentially no usable documentation.
